observation.visible_scene: A split-level (half-submerged) view of clear blue water under a pale sky. The upper band shows the sky, brightest on the right; the lower band shows the seabed lit by a shifting web of sunlight caustics on a dark teal floor. A curved water-surface line separates the two, with the rippled, mirror-like underside of the surface visible just below the skyline. A few tiny dark suspended specks sit in the mid-water on the left.
visible_changes: The water-surface arc continuously changes shape and thickness: early frames show a thin, smooth crest bulging near the top, while later frames show a broader, more heavily rippled band of surface reflection occupying more vertical space, indicating waves passing under the viewpoint.
The bright caustic net on the seabed shimmers and deforms slightly from frame to frame, with the lattice lines shifting position rather than the floor itself moving.
The skyline/waterline drifts vertically and tilts a little across the sequence, consistent with a floating or bobbing viewpoint.
A faint distant coastline with small structures, plus a tiny dark mark (possibly a distant boat), becomes visible on the left horizon in the later frames, absent at the start.
The small dark suspended particles in the mid-water remain in roughly the same relative positions throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the wave motion and of the camera's bobbing.
Whether the viewpoint is held by a person, a boat, or a rig, and what happens before/after the excerpt.
The true identity and distance of the horizon mark and coastline.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent vertical/tilt drift of the horizon is camera motion or physical wave motion cannot be separated cleanly.
The exact nature of the mid-water specks (particles vs. small organisms) is not determinable.
The caustic pattern's apparent movement could be partly refractive (surface waves) rather than object motion.
